content:
Alex G.: heads-up — multiple customers reporting SSE disconnects and partial streams from eu-west-1 since ~11:58 UTC. tickets coming in: 98712, 98715. customers say they get a few tokens then stream ends, client retries and sees duplicate tokens on reconnect. high volume between 11:58–12:10 UTC.
Maria H.: oncall here, I'm seeing increased stream-close rates in monitoring. error spike on ingress LB: 502/gateway-err and a cluster of EPIPEs in runtime logs.
Devin L.: copying runtime logs now. snippet from inference-runtime (eu-west-1):
```
[2026-11-05T11:59:04Z] runtime: connection id=0x7cfd closed: write EPIPE
[2026-11-05T11:59:04Z] proxy: upstream idle timeout, client reconnect attempt
[2026-11-05T12:00:03Z] model-server: kvcache miss, warmup triggered
[2026-11-05T12:01:22Z] auth: token-validate latency=180ms
```
Devin L.: also seeing a pattern where clients reconnect quickly which leads to duplicated first-chunk tokens because we stream partial tokens and client replays the same prompt.
Sophie K.: support reports customers seeing auth failures intermittently too, some 401s during the event window. Could be related if token validation is timing out.
Alex G.: customers want ETA and a mitigation. can we failover traffic to a healthy region or force fallback to a smaller model (eg: rdx-small-v1) while we investigate?
Devin L.: proposing immediate mitigations:
- enable route-level fallback to us-west-2 for new SSE streams (temporarily)
- reduce max-concurrent-sse-per-host to 50% on eu-west frontends
- for affected customers, flip to non-streaming (polling) endpoint if they accept it
I'll prepare commands.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20261105-34 (SSE partial streams eu-west). Pager notified.
statusbot: Status page updated: "Degradation: SSE streaming in eu-west-1. Customers may see disconnects and partial outputs. Engineers investigating."
Devin L.: runbook commands to apply immediate routing rule (internal):
```
# route new SSE traffic away from eu-west
rictl route update --service inference-sse --match region=eu-west-1 --set fallback_region=us-west-2 --priority=10

# throttle frontends
rictl frontend update --cluster eu-west-1 --set max_sse_conns=1200
```
Devin L.: and to force model fallback for canary customers:
```
rictl policy apply --customer 98712 --policy '{"sse_fallback_model":"rdx-small-v1","keepalive":15}'
```
Maria H.: I'm pushing the route update now and throttling frontends. will monitor for improvement.
Sophie K.: letting the customers know we applied temporary failover and asking if they can test connections. sending targeted DM updates.
Alex G.: reproduction steps for engineering and for support to verify:
1) open SSE with curl:
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rdx-large-v1","prompt":"hi","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```
2) after receiving first chunk, kill connection at client side and reconnect immediately. observe duplicated initial tokens on reconnect.
3) to capture server side, tail runtime logs on ingesters and model-server for the connection id printed in access logs.

Devin L.: after applying route update at 12:05 UTC, ingress errors dropped ~70% in the first 3m. still seeing occasional EPIPEs but fewer.
Maria H.: auth 401s decreased after token validation cache tweak (increased cache TTL from 5s -> 30s) at 12:08 UTC.
Sophie K.: customer 98712 confirming reduced disconnects but still seeing partial token duplication on rare reconnects.
Alex G.: temporary customer-facing triage note: "We’ve routed new streaming requests from eu-west-1 to us-west-2 and enabled a fallback model profile to reduce warmup impact. If you continue to experience truncated streams, try setting stream=false or reconnect with a 200ms jitter."
ops-bot: Alert suppressed for INC-20261105-34 (manual).
statusbot: Status page updated: "Mitigation in place: traffic failover and fallback models applied. Investigating root cause."
Devin L.: next steps I have on my list:
- dig into LB connection resets and kernel-level socket stats in eu-west fleet
- audit recent routing changes and autoscaler churn between 11:50–12:00 UTC
- add server-side idempotency marker for first-chunk tokens to avoid duplication on reconnection

Sophie K.: support action items: reach out to top-10 affected customers with repro steps, include temporary workaround (non-streaming), offer credits if SLA impacted.
Alex G.: will schedule a post-incident review once root cause is clear. please capture timestamps, customer repro, logs and the config changes we applied.
Maria H.: marking as "mitigated" for now since user-facing errors are much lower. setting a follow-up at 15:00 UTC to review logs and rollback/fine-tune throttles.
Support Bot: Noted: tickets 98712, 98715 updated with mitigation steps and customer messages.
Alex G.: thanks everyone — keep this thread updated with any regressions.
Sophie K.: adding final note for RC: consider adding a graceful stream resumption protocol or an idempotent event id on first-chunk to prevent duplicates on reconnect.
Alex G.: resolved at 12:30 UTC for major impact; follow-up investigation assigned to Devin.
